cond_0001.intro:
This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment.
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Preferred Requirements:
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.

cond_0105.intro: This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. A regular part of this role involves staying in contact with undergraduate assistants, Graduate Teaching Assistants, and a diverse student body. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents.
cond_0105.responsibilities:
Prepare culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses.
Run and maintain preparatory lab areas and equipment, including purchasing needed materials.
Actively assist with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, communicating regularly with instructors across sections to keep things consistent.
Assume the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable.
Assist with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses.
Supervise and train undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants, staying in ongoing contact to guide their work.
Work standing and sitting for extended periods, lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, and work up to two hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95–98° F.
Work with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms in an environment that includes equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C.

Two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.

Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Ability to work closely with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students, and to communicate clearly and comfortably with a diverse student body.
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.
Excellent communication skills with a diverse student body.
Ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.

cond_0116.intro: This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also takes ownership of running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment.
cond_0116.responsibilities:
Lead preparation of culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology lab courses.
Manage prep lab operations, including purchasing materials needed for culture media and reagent preparation.
Drive standardization of teaching methods and course materials across all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory.
Assume the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable.
Oversee teaching microbiology laboratory courses and direct the supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
Operate laboratory equipment and execute basic microbiology techniques.
Maintain effective communication with a diverse student body.
Work in an environment where temperature can reach 95-98° F for up to two hours at a time, handling a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms, including equipment with surface temperatures up to 350° C.
Lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, and work standing and sitting for extended periods.

Two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories (post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience).
Ability to operate laboratory equipment.
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Preferred Requirements**
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.

The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
cond_0127.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment.
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Preferred Requirements:
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.

The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
cond_0169.responsibilities:
Prepare culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses
Run and maintain preparatory lab areas and equipment
Purchase materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents
Monitor and standardize teaching methods and course materials across sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory
Assume duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable
Assist with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses
Supervise and train undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants
Handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques
Communicate with a diverse student body as required by lab operations
Coordinate with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants on assigned tasks
cond_0169.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories (post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience)
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines and work under pressure
Ability to operate laboratory equipment
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction
Ability to work with teaching laboratory personnel and students
Preferred Requirements:
Master's in Microbiology or related field
Three years of teaching laboratory experience
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel
Experience managing prep lab operations

The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. Most people become stronger in this kind of microbiology lab work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0203.responsibilities:
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
Special Instructions to Applicants
For full consideration please submit a cover letter, resume, and a list of three professional references by 4/24/24. However, applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled.
cond_0203.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment.
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Preferred Requirements
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.

cond_0247.intro: This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the microbiology techniques and lab preparation work involved.
cond_0247.responsibilities:
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
Special Instructions to Applicants
For full consideration please submit a cover letter, resume, and a list of three professional references by 4/24/24. However, applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled.
cond_0247.requirements:
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience. Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment. Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques. General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment. Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction. Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Master's in Microbiology or related field. Three years of teaching laboratory experience. Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel. Experience managing prep lab operations.

This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
cond_0353.requirements:
Minimum two years of demonstrated expertise in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Proven ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Strong command of laboratory equipment operation. Advanced knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques. Solid understanding of audio/visual classroom equipment. Expertise in laboratory classroom instruction. Exceptional ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Master's in Microbiology or related field required; advanced degree or additional specialization strongly preferred. Minimum three years of teaching laboratory experience. Substantial experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel. Proven track record managing prep lab operations.

cond_0384.intro: This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. A regular part of this role involves staying in contact with undergraduate assistants, Graduate Teaching Assistants, and a diverse student body. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents.
cond_0384.responsibilities:
Prepare culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses.
Run and maintain preparatory lab areas and equipment, including purchasing needed materials.
Actively assist with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials across all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, communicating regularly with instructors to flag inconsistencies and align approaches.
Assume the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable.
Assist with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses.
Supervise and train undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants, staying in ongoing contact to guide their work.
Work standing and sitting for extended periods, lift a minimum of 35 pounds, and climb ladders as needed.
Work up to two hours at a time in an environment where temperatures can reach 95–98°F, and handle a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms, including equipment with surface temperatures up to 350°C.
cond_0384.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories (post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience).
Ability to operate laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work both autonomously and collaboratively, and handle pressure.
Strong communication skills with a diverse student body and comfort working closely with teaching laboratory personnel and students on a daily basis.
Preferred Requirements
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel, including proactively initiating guidance and feedback.
Experience managing prep lab operations.

This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as clear written and direct verbal communication with a diverse student body and the ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.

cond_0406.intro:
This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.

cond_0516.intro:
This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
For full consideration please submit a cover letter, resume, and a list of three professional references by 4/24/24. However, applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled.
cond_0516.requirements:
Around two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Familiarity with laboratory equipment and a working knowledge of basic microbiology techniques. General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment. Some background in laboratory classroom instruction. Willingness to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.

The Lab Technician works closely with the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator and is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also shares responsibility for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes coordinating the purchasing of materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and works alongside undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants in their supervision and training. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
cond_0540.requirements:
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience. Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment. Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques. General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment. Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction. Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Master's in Microbiology or related field. Three years of teaching laboratory experience. Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel. Experience managing prep lab operations.

Background checks will be conducted when required by law or contract and when, in the discretion of the university, it is reasonable and prudent to do so.

cond_0619.intro:
This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.

This person also is responsible for running and maintaining preparatory lab areas and equipment. Maintenance of the prep lab includes purchasing materials needed for preparation of culture media and reagents. The Lab Tech assists with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory. This person assumes the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable. The tech assists with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses and supervision and training of undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. This position requires the ability to handle laboratory equipment and perform basic microbiology techniques, as well as excellent communication skills with a diverse student body and ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with microbiology lab preparation and teaching support.
cond_0644.responsibilities:
The tech must be able to work two (2) hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95-98° F. The tech works with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms. The environment includes exposures such as equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C. The employee must be able to lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, work standing and sitting for extended periods of time.
Special Instructions to Applicants
For full consideration please submit a cover letter, resume, and a list of three professional references by 4/24/24. However, applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled.
cond_0644.requirements:
Two years experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience. Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment. Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques. General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment. Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction. Ability to work with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students.
Master's in Microbiology or related field. Three years of teaching laboratory experience. Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel. Experience managing prep lab operations.

cond_0645.intro: This position reports to and supports the Teaching Laboratory Coordinator. The Lab Technician is primarily responsible for preparing culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses, including Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, Pathogenic Microbiology Laboratory, and other laboratory courses as needed. A regular part of this role involves staying in contact with undergraduate assistants, Graduate Teaching Assistants, and a diverse student body. cond_0645.responsibilities:
Prepare culture media, reagents, and cultures for microbiology laboratory courses.
Run and maintain preparatory lab areas and equipment, including purchasing needed materials.
Actively assist with monitoring and standardizing teaching methods and course materials among all sections of Introduction to Microbiology Laboratory, communicating regularly with instructors across sections to keep things consistent.
Assume the duties of Teaching Lab Coordinator when that person is unavailable.
Assist with oversight of teaching microbiology laboratory courses.
Supervise and train undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants, staying in ongoing contact to guide their work.
Work standing and sitting for extended periods, lift a minimum of 35 pounds, climb ladders, and work up to two hours at a time in an environment where the temperature can reach 95–98° F.
Work with a wide range of chemicals and living microbial organisms in an environment that includes equipment posing burn danger with surface temperatures to 350° C.
cond_0645.requirements:
Two years of experience in research and/or higher education teaching laboratories. Post-secondary research training may be substituted for experience.
Ability to organize workload effectively to meet deadlines, work autonomously and collaboratively, and under pressure.
Ability to operate laboratory equipment.
Knowledge of and ability to perform basic microbiology techniques.
General knowledge of audio/visual classroom equipment.
Proficiency in laboratory classroom instruction.
Ability to work closely with others, including teaching laboratory personnel and students, and to communicate clearly and comfortably with a diverse student body.
Master's in Microbiology or related field.
Three years of teaching laboratory experience.
Experience supervising and training teaching lab personnel.
Experience managing prep lab operations.
Excellent communication skills with a diverse student body.
Ability to work effectively with undergraduate assistants and Graduate Teaching Assistants.
